clue.text: Playmate carrying one bucket …

indicators.note: a word that carries another holds it within itself, so the playmate holds the one

parts.note: a pal is a friend or playmate
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A child's friend brings along a seaside bucket, the ellipsis carrying the story on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name an open container with a handle for carrying water.

clue.text: Such Scots breathe convulsively or pech at first climbing trunk

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: sic is the Scots word for such
to sob is to draw breath in spasms

indicators.note: the opening letter of pech is taken; pech is Scots for pant

explanation.surface: Scots gasp and pant as they climb up a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC + SOB + OR + P read upwards gives the answer. Pech is a Scots verb meaning to pant.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's long flexible nose is its trunk, and the zoological word names exactly that.

clue.text: Playing tennis with Federer essentially I'm concentrated

indicators.note: playing with letters puts them in a fresh order
the essence is the central letter of the name Federer

explanation.surface: A player facing Roger Federer says he is focused hard on the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' shuffles TENNIS into INTENS; 'essentially' takes the middle E of FEDERER. 'I'm' only sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong or highly focused state, as in intense effort, is a concentrated one.

clue.text: … can run out and start to weep for a hit on the head

indicators.note: the new letters stand for the A of the first word, taking its place

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word weep is used

explanation.surface: Continuing from the bucket: a can runs dry, and someone cries after being struck on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the A in CAN for RO plus W (the first letter of 'weep'); 'for a' signals that swap.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown someone is informal for striking them on the top of the skull, the crown being that part.

clue.text: When what confronts you's accepted for men it can hinder progress

indicators.note: the new letters take the place of the ones for men

parts.note: the puzzle in front of the solver is a crossword
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers or men
in means accepted or fashionable

explanation.surface: When the opposition is welcomed among the troops, it slows the advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'you's' as 'you has'. OR, other ranks, is a crossword convention for men; 'for' signals the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing across one's path pushes a vehicle or aircraft sideways and slows its advance.

clue.text: Only child runs about to be in time for Hallowe'en

indicators.note: the first letters go about the second piece, enclosing it

parts.note: OC is an abbreviation for only child
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An only child hurries around to be on time for Hallowe'en.
explanation.walkthrough: TO BE sits inside OC + R.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowe'en falls on the last day of the tenth month, so the month is when it happens.

clue.text: Very much what ring and Marciano have in common

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning greatly or a lot, as in pleased beyond measure

definitions.text: what ring and Marciano have in common
definitions.meaning: a ring is a circle without a finish, and the boxer Marciano's name finishes in NO

explanation.surface: A boxing ring and the boxer Rocky Marciano share something important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' and 'Marciano' suggest boxing, but a ring is a circle with no end, and MARCIANO ends in NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means immensely, as in 'that pleased her greatly'.

clue.text: Man with 3 presided going over work?

indicators.note: going over turns the pieces back on themselves, so they are written right to left

parts.note: the chess king is the man shown wearing a crown (3 across); K is its abbreviation
sat, as a judge sits to preside over a court

explanation.surface: A man who wears the crown has chaired a meeting and is reviewing a piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' refers to the answer to 3 across, CROWN. K and SAT together are KSAT, and turned round they give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A job or assignment is a piece of work; the question mark admits the definition is broad.

clue.text: Done with what originally should come before reading say in 'Educating Rita'?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed ahead of the next piece
the letters are changed from their original order

parts.note: reading is one of the three Rs, so R

explanation.surface: A finished task needs to be read through, as in the play about an Open University student.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange DONE WHAT into TWOHANDE and add R; reading is one of the three Rs. 'Educating Rita' is a play with only two characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Russell's play has just two roles, the tutor and Rita, so it is an example of such a piece.

clue.text: Old line one found separating shillings from pence, unserviceable for example

definitions.text: Old line one found separating shillings from pence, unserviceable for example

indicators.note: the three letters are set between the two money abbreviations

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shillings, as in old British money
D, from the Latin denarius, is the old abbreviation for pence
I is the Roman numeral for one
US is the abbreviation for unserviceable, written with a slash as U/S

explanation.surface: An old ledger line separating shillings from pence, as in the abbreviation for unusable.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money had shillings and pence, written like 3/10; the slash is this mark. 'for example' points to U/S, which contains one.
explanation.definitionFit: The oblique stroke used in old money notation and in U/S is the slash, which typographers call by this name.

clue.text: Exuberant forces hold on to power retaining fort

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep the fort's abbreviation held inside them
to force something is to wrench it out of its shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Military forces cling to power and keep hold of a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forces' looks like a noun in the military picture, but it is the signal to rearrange the four-word phrase, and 'retaining' puts the fort's abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone feeling elated and in high spirits is said to be at the summit of the globe.

clue.text: They possess tranquillisers that are out of date

indicators.note: the date's abbreviation is taken out of the drug word

parts.note: downers is slang for sedative drugs

explanation.surface: Someone holds a stock of sedatives that have passed their expiry date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of date' reads as expired, but it says remove D from DOWNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who possess things are their proprietors, the holders of title to property.

clue.text: Jumper Jonathan put on heading for break — and for a lie-down

indicators.note: the jumper's surname is placed on after that letter
only the leading letter of the word break is taken

parts.note: Jonathan Edwards is the British triple jumper, world record holder

explanation.surface: An athlete puts on a sweater as he heads off on a break, ready to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is not clothing but Jonathan Edwards, the British triple-jump champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means towards bed, which is where one goes to rest or lie down.

clue.text: Coughing more? Withdraw — it's interrupting entertainment

indicators.note: the turned letters break into the entertainment word

parts.note: cheer in the sense of food and drink provided, good cheer

indicators.note: to withdraw is to draw back, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone coughing worse is told to leave because the noise is spoiling a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' makes STI; 'Coughing more?' looks like part of the story but is the definition, with chesty meaning prone to coughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesty describes a cough or cold settled on the lungs, so the comparative suits a person coughing more.

clue.text: Suspect real malts must be on the rocks

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is on the rocks, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Genuine single malts ought to be served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' seems to mean with ice but rearranges REAL MALTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to sense something is wrong is to suspect foul play.

clue.text: Fashionable Gaelic festival is hard to follow

indicators.note: the letter for hard is told to come after the preceding pieces

parts.note: the Mod is the annual Scottish Gaelic festival of music and literature
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A trendy Highland cultural festival proves difficult to keep up with.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mod is Scotland's annual Gaelic arts festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight synonym: something stylish and in vogue is described this way.

clue.text: Until that time when e-mail fails

indicators.note: a failing system breaks down, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Waiting until a moment when the email system breaks down.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb for the interval before something happens, in the intervening period.

clue.text: The Queen has introduced one over a year in a network of vast range

indicators.note: in a down entry the first part sits over the next
the Queen's letters take in another letter between them

parts.note: HM, Her Majesty
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the article and the year go in the article and network

parts.note: LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: The monarch has opened a vast network spanning more than a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has introduced' and 'in' give HIM and ALAYAN; 'range' looks like a network's reach but means mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names the world's highest mountain range, so a vast range is described this way.

clue.text: Hide that's left among hides to be tanned

indicators.note: the letter for left sits among the shuffled letters
tanning works a hide into new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An animal skin that was set aside sits with others waiting for the tannery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be tanned' rearranges HIDES into SHIED, with L placed among them.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to screen or protect it from view, a verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Sensationally fired Jack at Jill

parts.note: Jack stands for any man, so he
Jill stands for any woman, so her

explanation.surface: A sensational firing: Jack was let go for his treatment of Jill.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an allusion to the idiom 'set the heather on fire', meaning to cause a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the moorland shrub alight is the idiom for causing a stir, so the plant is what sensationally burns.

clue.text: Conference area guides come to harm without me

indicators.note: guides steer something into a new course, so these letters are rearranged
the letters of me are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: Guides make sure nobody comes to grief, leaving the speaker out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M and E from the letters of COME TO HARM and rearrange the rest, the signal being 'guides'.
explanation.definitionFit: An online forum where users talk in real time is a virtual meeting place for discussion.

clue.text: Stun prisoner on oath

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece is placed on top of the other

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
a cuss is a swear word or oath

explanation.surface: A prisoner swears, and the oath is stunning.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone senseless by a blow to the head is to stun them.

clue.text: Intent to leave flat purchase with promise of house to come?

definitions.meaning: a scheme for going away, a plan to be gone

definitions.text: flat purchase with promise of house to come?
definitions.meaning: buying property from drawings before it has been built

explanation.surface: A buyer meaning to move out purchases a flat while expecting a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, it is a plan to go away; as a property term it means buying before construction.

clue.text: Plan foul to foil attack …

indicators.note: to foil a plan is to upset it, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A treacherous scheme is drawn up to thwart an assault, the ellipsis linking to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to set upon someone suddenly, an assault.

clue.text: Standard say of flimsiness?

definitions.meaning: the London Evening Standard is an example of a newspaper
something thin and flimsy is described as being like a sheet of it

explanation.surface: A question about what standard of flimsiness is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Evening Standard is a London newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is commonly called by this name; as an adjective it means thin and weak, like paper walls.

clue.text: … Sorry. We foul to order

indicators.note: putting things to order sorts them into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: An apology follows: we committed a foul on command.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry in its sense of pitiful or wretched, as in a sorry sight, means the same.

clue.text: They will frame a picture to be restored from start to finish in tender fashion

indicators.note: the first word goes round the other pieces like a frame round a painting
a restored painting is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: from start to finish means the whole thing, all of it

explanation.surface: Restorers will mount a painting once it has been completely restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be restored' makes RAPEUTIC; 'tender' means tending the sick, not soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender is used in the sense of tending or caring for the sick, which therapy does.

clue.text: Start out regularly to jog

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of the words that precede it

explanation.surface: Setting off at a steady pace, as a runner does when starting to jog.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle run at a moderate pace, like a horse's gait between a walk and a canter.

clue.text: Creature prized for fragrance, mount required for entry to Jerusalem in Scripture

indicators.note: the mount sits in the letters for scripture

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject of scripture

parts.words: mount required for entry to Jerusalem
parts.note: Jesus rode a donkey, an ass, into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling animal and the beast ridden into Jerusalem in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a small Asian civet whose scent glands yield civet perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: This small civet cat is valued for the musky secretion used in perfumery.

clue.text: One number divided by another provides solution immediately

indicators.note: the second abbreviation splits the first pair apart

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing
another number, here NO, the other abbreviation of number

explanation.surface: An arithmetic sum: dividing one figure by another gives the answer at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided by' is not arithmetic: NO, a second abbreviation for number, sits between A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning soon or straight away, as in 'I'll be there presently'.
